meta.title: Crowd Crush at the VerrowFest Venue
meta.subtitle: Crowd-safety major incident | Thornlea Park, Verrow | Time unspecified

bullets.text: A crowd crush and serious disorder were reported around the front standing area of the VerrowFest main stage.
People moved away from the barrier area as evacuation activity developed at the venue.
Multiple injury reports included an eyewitness account that at least six people were carried from the front pen unconscious.
Emergency, police, crowd-safety, and hospital responders were mobilized while warnings and service disruptions were reported.
Initial reports indicated an evolving problem in the front standing area and front pen.
People began moving away while early reports described evacuation activity around the barriers.

bullets.text: Unspecified earlier developments occurred before the incident was reported at the barriers.
Early evacuation reports were explicitly unclear or framed as reports before later confirmation.
Several injury reports remained unconfirmed or described only as possible.
Multiple posts offered vague or explicitly unconfirmed updates about the front area without substantive details.
Initial service-disruption claims were framed as incoming reports before later confirmation.
The developments said to have preceded the barrier incident were not identified.
The reports provide no exact incident time or verified account of what caused the crowd crush.
No verified total for fatalities, injuries, missing people, or trapped people is provided.
The affected service and the duration of its disruption are not identified.
Twenty-four signal tweets presented claims as official, confirmed, or attributable to public-response organizations.
Four signal tweets contained direct eyewitness material or redistributed a specific eyewitness account.
Thirty-four signal tweets were retweets, increasing repetition without necessarily adding independent corroboration.
Seventeen signal tweets used hedged, hearsay, possible, reportedly, or explicitly unconfirmed wording.
The claim that at least six people were carried out unconscious appeared in three tweets, including two retweets.
Service-disruption information appeared in eight tweets, progressing from incoming reports to confirmed notices.
Warning information appeared in seven tweets, progressing from reports of a warning to confirmation and guidance.
Operational information progressed from reports of crews responding to confirmed deployment and a police major-incident declaration.
